1	# SUBMISSION
     2	
     3	## Concept
     4	
     5	**Enterprise:** The pit-to-concentrator chain of an open-pit copper mine: three faces, the shovels and 227 t trucks that serve them, the haul-road network, the primary crusher, the ROM pad, the coarse ore stockpile, the concentrator feed, the waste dump, the diesel fuel bay and the site power supply. The flotation circuit itself is not modelled; the concentrator is the feed it receives and the copper it recovers.
     6	
     7	**Users:** The shift dispatcher, the maintenance planner and the site energy engineer, looking at one control-room view.
     8	
     9	**Decision:** Whether to accept an operating change, or to leave the mine as it is. A change is a failed crusher, a closed road, a shovel out of service, harder or lower-grade ore, a fuel shortage, a grid cap, or switching off dispatch, maintenance or energy management. The twin runs a second, identical mine that does not take the change. The decision is the difference in copper, plant feed, queue time, availability, kWh/t and diesel L/t.
    10	
    11	**Why this choice:** In this chain those quantities move together. Ore that cannot enter the crusher goes to the ROM pad, the coarse ore stockpile then drains, and the concentrator starves. A harder face slows the shovel and raises crusher kWh/t. A grid cap can be met by throttling the concentrator or by tripping it, and the two choices do not yield the same copper. The second mine uses the same seed and the same random draw for each machine, so the difference is the change, not luck.
    12	
    13	**Real or fictional:** The site is fictional. It resembles a porphyry copper open pit with a gyratory primary crusher and a concentrator fed from a coarse ore stockpile. Truck and shovel sizes follow public class specification sheets (Caterpillar 793F, Komatsu PC5500, Caterpillar 6060, Liebherr R 9600). Copper grades, Bond work indices and recovery follow the open GeoMet dataset (Hoffimann et al. 2022, CC BY 4.0). Pit geometry, fleet size, stockpiles, the failure model and the grid cap are synthetic; every value and its source is listed in `twinvision/DATA_ASSUMPTIONS.md`.

    23	**TwinVision Copper Pit** is a fictional open-pit copper mine in Kazakhstan, together with its primary crushing and concentrator feed. It covers the value chain from the blasted face to copper in concentrate:
    24	
    25	- block clusters are dug by shovels;
    26	- haul trucks carry the material over a road graph to the crusher, the ROM pad or the waste dump;
    27	- the crusher fills the coarse ore stockpile;
    28	- the stockpile feeds the concentrator.
    29	
    30	Diesel comes from a fuel bay, electricity from a capped grid connection, and machines wear, fail and are maintained.
    31

   145	
   146	- **Real data.** The open GeoMet dataset (Hoffimann et al. 2022, Zenodo record 7051975, CC BY 4.0) is included unmodified in `twinvision/data/geomet/`, with checksums.    148	- **Synthetic.** The following are synthetic and labelled as such: the mine itself, its location, pit geometry, road network, the spatial pattern of the block model, fleet size, stockpile sizes, plant target, fuel logistics, failure and maintenance parameters, and the grid cap.
   149	- **No sensitive data.** No confidential or personal data is used.
   150	- **Details.** [`twinvision/DATA_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](twinvision/DATA_ASSUMPTIONS.md) lists every parameter with its value and source; [`DATA_LICENSES.md`](DATA_LICENSES.md) covers licences; [`twinvision/DECISIONS.md`](twinvision/DECISIONS.md) explains the design choices.

   152	## Mine visualization
   153	
   154	**Live mine map: http://localhost:8095/.** No login is needed. It opens with moving trucks and needs no clicks.
   155	
   156	- **Map.** A 2D SVG map refreshed every second from Ditto. It shows:
   157	  - pit benches and block clusters coloured by copper grade, with dug blocks faded;
   158	  - roads (closed ones in red);
   159	  - shovels and trucks coloured by state, with load-grade dots and health rings;
   160	  - the crusher, stockpile fill levels, the concentrator with feed-grade status, the waste dump and the fuel bay;
   161	  - failed or closed items pulsing red, and optional dashed baseline "ghost" trucks.
   162	- **Views and inspector.** Mine, Pit and Plant views are available. Clicking any object shows its Ditto thing, live next to baseline.
   163	- **Header and gauges.** The header shows the Ditto connection, the live mass, fuel and energy balance badges, and the active what-ifs or switched-off modules. Below the map are gauges with baseline markers and machine health cards.
   164	- **Right panel.** It shows 11 KPIs live vs baseline with deltas (t/h, ore, plant feed, feed grade, copper, queue time, availability, crusher and site kWh/t, diesel L/t, 15-minute grid demand), an InfluxDB trend of the selected KPI and the event log.
   165	
   166	**Grafana: http://localhost:3000/d/twinvision-overview.** The dashboard "TwinVision Copper Pit – live vs baseline" pairs a live and a baseline series for every KPI, the balance residuals and maintenance/reliability. The twin hierarchy is under Grafana → OpenEgiz app → Twins.
   167	
   168	## Limitations
   169	
   170	- **Map.** It is 2D only; there is no Unity scene.
   171	- **Fictional site.** The mine is fictional. Only the grade, hardness and recovery distributions come from real data; the spatial pattern of the block model is synthetic.
   172	- **Concentrator model.** The concentrator is a feed sink with Bond energy and a constant recovery. There are no flotation or grinding circuit dynamics, and no concentrate or tailings handling.
   173	- **Fixed fleet.** The fleet is fixed (8 trucks, 3 shovels), and there is one crusher and one dump.
   174	- **Restarts.** The simulator does not persist its state: after a container restart both copies start again from simulated time 0, which keeps them comparable. The undo history is held in memory by the web service; the scenario state itself is stored in Ditto and survives restarts.
   175	- **KPI averaging.** KPIs are 30-minute moving averages in simulated time (about 90 s of real time at the default 20× speed), so effects build up over a minute or two.
   176	- **Simplified energy cap.** The grid cap acts on the concentrator only, and load shedding is modelled as a fixed 15-minute trip.
   177	- **Lab-tested clean start.** The clean start was verified in an arm64 container that mirrors the judging setup; amd64 is covered by the CI workflow.
